data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is primarily governed by a humidity-emissivity feedback, where urban dryness alters longwave emissivity and suppresses cooling, and the gap is larger in more humid regional climates.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If intense urban irrigation maintains humidity levels equal to the rural surroundings, the emissivity feedback is neutralized.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If both urban and rural environments are extremely arid, the baseline humidity is too low for any significant differential emissivity effect to manifest.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Differential near-surface humidity and its feedback on longwave emissivity govern the UHI.
